clue.text: Rowing coach's instruction at start of Oxbridge do?

parts.note: at means in, as in 'at home' or 'in the house'

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of Oxbridge

parts.note: UT is the old name for the first note of the scale, now usually doh or do

explanation.surface: A question about what a rowing coach shouts at the beginning of a university boat event.
explanation.walkthrough: The coach calls the rhythm of the oars going in and out of the water. 'start of' takes the first letter of Oxbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaches call the stroke rhythm to rowers, telling them when blades enter and leave the water.

clue.text: Beginning nice pint one's ordered

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the possessive adds no letter

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so these letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone orders a nice pint at the start of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' signals the anagram of NICE and PINT, giving NCIPIENT, with I (one) in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient is an adjective for something just starting to emerge or develop.

clue.text: Eg eight rowers etc tote around…

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A crew of eight rowers and their kit are carried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the anagram of ETC and TOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An octette is any group of eight, and a rowing eight is one example.

clue.text: …three that row in Oxford primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so take the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Continuing the rowing scene: three people who row at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letters of 'that row in Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three people or things.

clue.text: Mature lover losing head with fellow in enclosure

indicators.note: in signals that the lover and fellow are placed within the enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: Romeo, Shakespeare's lover, is the byword for an ardent suitor

explanation.surface: An older lover, now headless, is shut in a pen with another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts the R from ROMEO, leaving OMEO; add F and put the lot 'in' CAGE after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To come of age is to reach adulthood, so it serves as a verb meaning grow up.

clue.text: Putting wrong interpretation on string music maybe?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged differently, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a phrase about music for strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals the anagram of ON, STRING and MUSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Misconstruing is understanding or explaining something incorrectly.

clue.text: Cry of pain when losing a bit of composure in bed

indicators.note: losing means the following letter is dropped from the word for bed

parts.note: a couch is a bed or sofa to lie on

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter, from composure

explanation.surface: Someone lying down loses their calm and cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of composure' is C; 'losing' takes it from COUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation people shout when they are suddenly hurt.

clue.text: Electrical phenomena around poles or in occult emanations

indicators.note: in places the small word or within the word for the emanations

parts.note: auras are subtle glows said by mystics to surround people

explanation.surface: Polar lights are described, with a choice between science and the occult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OR inside AURAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern and southern lights are glowing displays caused by charged particles near the polar regions.

clue.text: Try to write a letter, yes?

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
ay or aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to attempt writing a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write' is a link; the surface pretends the answer is something written, a fair second hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something, as a verb, is to attempt it.

clue.text: Row in place of porgy!

parts.note: read as the street (Row) that is the setting of Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess, rather than a quarrel or a fish

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out instead of a fish being served.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera Porgy and Bess is set in a tenement street called ___ Row in Charleston; the fish porgy and the 'row' tempt you towards angling.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional street in the Gershwin opera is named after a whiskered fish.

clue.text: Disturbed that other lion not far behind

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A second lion, upset, is following closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' signals the anagram of THAT, OTHER and LION.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a pursuer close to catching what they chase.

clue.text: Here's a plant, see, growing wild out east!

definitions.text: Here's a plant, see, growing wild out east!

indicators.note: growing wild suggests the letters sprouting in a disordered new arrangement

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A gardener points out a plant running riot in the eastern beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' scrambles HERES A PLANT SEE, and 'out' removes the E for east from that pool; the whole clue also describes the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant's ears are large-leaved plants such as colocasia or bergenia, named for their huge leaves.

clue.text: Quarrelled as I'd got up with desire to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the desire after the reversed words
in a down entry got up means the words are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the words as I'd, taken letter for letter without the apostrophe
greed is an excessive desire

explanation.surface: Someone argued after rising, driven by longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns AS I'D into DISA; 'to follow' puts GREED after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to differ in opinion, and the past tense can mean argued.

clue.text: She twice pressed around women like Chloe

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
twice means the word she is used two times

explanation.surface: A woman squeezes round to describe pastoral heroines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles SHE and 'around' signals the anagram of SHESHE plus PRESSED. Chloe is the shepherdess heroine of the Greek romance Daphnis and Chloe.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe in the pastoral romance tends flocks, so girls like her are female sheep-minders.

clue.text: Likely to fix market

parts.note: to set something is to fix it in place
a fair is a market or show

explanation.surface: A trader seems ready to rig the market.
explanation.walkthrough: SET FAIR is a weather-forecast term for settled, hence likely to go well.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes a situation, like settled weather, that promises a good outcome.

clue.text: Saint with a besetting sin

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so sin encloses with

explanation.surface: A holy figure has one persistent weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besetting' puts WITH inside SIN. St Swithin's Day, 15 July, is the British legend of forty days of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Swithin was a ninth-century bishop of Winchester, venerated as a holy man.

clue.text: One who brings bad luck on entering uplifting pilgrimage

indicators.note: entering means the small word on goes inside the reversed pilgrimage
in a down entry uplifting means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the haj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A jinx joins an inspiring religious journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns HAJ into JAH; 'entering' puts ON inside after the J.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophet was thrown overboard as the cause of a storm, so the name means a jinx.

clue.text: Flight I board to attract attention

indicators.note: to board is to get on or into, so I goes inside the other word

parts.note: to star is to stand out and draw attention

explanation.surface: A passenger boards a flight to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' puts I into STAR; 'Flight' is a flight of steps, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight of steps, or the staircase itself.

clue.text: Clothes to boast about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for boast is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BRAG round.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing, especially distinctive dress.

clue.text: Lights losing source of current

indicators.note: losing its source means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: lamps are lights

explanation.surface: Lamps go out when the electricity supply fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing source' drops the L from LAMPS; 'current' is the definition, by way of its unit, amps.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current is measured in units named after Ampère, so the plural stands for current.

clue.text: Falls over artist once more outside

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole construction is read backwards
outside means the word for once more goes round the artist

parts.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter is tumbling again over a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts RA in AGAIN after its first A, giving ARAGAIN; 'over' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Detective sticks to house at start of evening

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

indicators.note: at the start of means take the first letter of evening

explanation.surface: An investigator stays at home as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at start of' gives E from evening. GUMSHOE is US slang for a private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumshoe is American slang for a private investigator, from soft-soled shoes.

clue.text: Flowers he'll see first outside are initially blue

indicators.note: outside means the first words wrap round the next ones

parts.note: he'll written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of blue
first takes the opening letter of see

explanation.surface: Someone will spot the first blue blooms outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: HELL plus S ('first' of see) goes 'outside' ARE and B ('initially' blue), split as H...ELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Harebells are bluebell-like wild flowers, the bluebells of Scotland.

clue.text: Peccadillo — peculiar, we hear, in ecclesiastical council

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a peccadillo is a small sin; odd means peculiar

explanation.surface: A minor scandal is rumoured to have occurred at a church assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says SIN ODD sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a governing assembly of church clergy and lay members.
